title: Newport Festivals and the New Jersey Jazz Society
summary: Leeman plays the first Newport Festival with Condon, who conducted under an umbrella in the rain, and later New York Newport and Waterloo Village concerts.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I must mention -- I did the first year of the Newport Festivals were starting, with Eddie Condon, for George Wein, Schroeder he was the promoter. We had Peanuts Hucko, Jack Lesberg, Gene Shrader, and Cutty Cutshall among others. And it rained

and it poured, and this great outdoor auditorium, and if you know anything about Eddie Condon, instead of playing the guitar, he took it upon himself to conduct the six pieces, and because of the rain which didn't cover the back, or the front of the show, where he announced, he had an umbrella over his head -- and it made quite a picture.

Since then, I've done many of the Newport Festivals, especially when they moved down to New York, and they call them now the New York Newport Festivals. I've done them with the World's Greatest Jazz Band, and I've done them especially with Eddie Condon. And the last couple of years, they've had a subsidiary that is part of the Newport Festival down in New Jersey. Sponsored by the New Jersey Jazz Society in connection with -- or I should say the New Jersey Jazz Society working hand in hand with George Wein. And presenting the New Jersey-New York Waterloo concerts at Waterloo Village. It's a 200 year old or more restored village that goes back to George Washington's time, that would be 1700 -- at Waterloo Village, New Jersey, and it's a beautiful background to jazz concerts.
